newsitem.title: UK: City of Bogota named best Latam syndicated loan.
newsitem.headline: City of Bogota named best Latam syndicated loan.

text.p: A landmark $195 million syndicated loan for the City of Bogota has won an International Financing Review (IFR) award for the best such financing in Latin America, the city's mayor said in a statement released in London.
"The International Financing Review...has just granted the City of Santa Fe de Bogota, capital of Colombia, its acknowledgement as the best (such) negotiation of the year 1996," the statement said.
The IFR is due to formally present the award for "Best Latin American Loan of the Year" later on Thursday.

The five-year loan, the first syndicated loan for a Latin American city, was arranged by ING Barings (U.S.) Securities and J.P. Morgan Securities. Launched in New York in November, it was priced at 175 basis points over three-month Libor.
It was increased to $195 million after an initial projection of $150 million, and was assigned a BBB rating by Standard & Poor's.
The proceeds are earmarked for financing infrastructure and social projects until 1998, and to initiate the planning of other projects until 2020, the statement said.
In making the award, IFR commended the arrangers for getting the S&P rating.
"Having the municipality rated, and investment grade at that, was key to making banks comfortable with joining the syndicated loan," it said in an article seen by Reuters ahead of publication.

It also highlighted the loan's innovative structure since it uses the city's tax revenues as security -- a structure rarely seen among international syndicated loans. --Caroline Brothers, London Newsroom +44 171 542 2734
